question: Assume today is 2026-09-05. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of new passenger cars (Pkw) registered in Germany in September 2026, as it will be first reported in the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt's (KBA) monthly press release on vehicle registrations.

target.what: New passenger car (Pkw) registrations in Germany during September 2026, counted as newly registered passenger cars (Neuzulassungen von Personenkraftwagen) in the KBA monthly vehicle-registrations release; excludes used-car re-registrations, production, and wholesale/retail sales unless they correspo
target.caveats: Working interpretation is KBA's 'Neuzulassungen von Personenkraftwagen' for Germany, all powertrains, private and commercial owners. Important alternatives: total motor vehicles (Kraftfahrzeuge), Pkw by powertrain, or ACEA's Germany series (which may ultimately use KBA as source). The target period

candidates.hypothesis: September Pkw registrations follow a stable seasonal pattern plus recent trend; target can be estimated from the latest 2026 monthly run-rate, year-ago September, and historical August-to-September and September-to-annual relationships, adjusted for working days.
candidates.data_to_find: KBA monthly Neuzulassungen von Personenkraftwagen for January 2018 through August 2026; September values for 2015-2025; August 2026 total; monthly working-day counts; any KBA revisions. Minimum evidence: recent September observations plus August 2026 and 2025-2026 monthly trend.

candidates.hypothesis: The September share of annual German Pkw registrations and September daily rate relative to annual average are stable enough to convert an annual 2026 forecast into a September 2026 estimate; working-day composition and special calendar effects must be applied.
candidates.data_to_find: Historical KBA annual and September Pkw Neuzulassungen, ideally 2010-2025; monthly working-day counts; September 2026 calendar composition; September share and daily-rate factors. Minimum evidence: 3-5 recent September shares and working-day data.
search_hints: KBA Pkw Neuzulassungen September Anteil Jahres 2024
Germany September share annual car registrations historical

candidates.hypothesis: A published 2026 annual forecast for German passenger car registrations, multiplied by the September seasonal share from d2, gives a usable target estimate; forecast vintage must be on or before 2026-09-05 and comparable in definition to KBA Pkw Neuzulassungen.
candidates.data_to_find: 2026 annual forecasts for Germany new passenger car registrations from VDA, S&P Global Mobility, ifo, ACEA, bank research, or industry associations, with publication dates before cutoff and scope definitions. Minimum evidence: one credible annual total forecast and its definition.
search_hints: Germany passenger car registrations forecast 2026 S&P Global Mobility

candidates.hypothesis: Domestic new Pkw registrations are approximately domestic production delivered in Germany plus new passenger car imports, after timing and inventory adjustments; production/export/import data and domestic-delivery shares can constrain the supply available for September registrations.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly German passenger car production, exports, imports, and domestic sales for 2023-August 2026; share of domestic production sold in Germany; new-car import statistics; any September 2026 production plans or order backlog. Minimum evidence: recent monthly production/import flows and a domestic-delivery bridge.
search_hints: VDA Pkw Produktion Export Inland August 2026
Germany passenger car production domestic sales monthly 2026

candidates.hypothesis: Near-term registrations are reflected in dealer order backlog, inventory, new orders, and business expectations; ifo Kfz-Gewerbe and dealer survey data can predict the September 2026 registration rate better than a pure seasonal extrapolation.
candidates.data_to_find: ifo Geschäftsklima Kfz-Gewerbe, new passenger-car order intake/backlog, dealer inventory days, and expected sales through August/early September 2026; historical relationship between these indicators and next-month KBA Pkw registrations. Minimum evidence: latest survey and one historical correlation or bridge.
search_hints: German car dealer order backlog September 2026

candidates.hypothesis: Private and commercial Pkw registrations respond to consumer confidence, real incomes, interest rates, unemployment, and GDP nowcasts; latest macro signals can adjust the seasonal-trend estimate for September 2026, especially if demand conditions shifted in 2026.
candidates.data_to_find: German consumer confidence, retail sales, unemployment, GDP nowcast, and auto-loan rates through August 2026; historical KBA split between private and commercial Pkw holders; estimated elasticities or simple directional adjustments. Minimum evidence: latest macro readings and historical private/commercial registration shares.
search_hints: German consumer confidence August 2026 car purchases
Pkw Neuzulassungen gewerbliche private Halter KBA 2025
Germany car registrations macro elasticity consumer confidence

candidates.hypothesis: Policy changes, incentives, tax treatment, CO2 rules, model launches, or supply disruptions can pull registrations forward or delay them around September 2026; any announced effective-date shock should be quantified by affected Pkw share and typical timing shift.
candidates.data_to_find: Announced German/EU automotive tax, subsidy, company-car, CO2, or registration-policy changes effective around September-October 2026; affected powertrain or buyer shares; historical evidence of registration pull-forward around similar announcements; new-model launch calendar. Minimum evidence: any material effective-date policy and affected share.
search_hints: German car registration pull forward policy September 2026

candidates.hypothesis: Correctly pinning the KBA definition and release vintage prevents mis-mapping from total motor vehicles, powertrain subsets, or ACEA series to the target; historical first-release versus revised values indicates reporting uncertainty but usually not a large level shift.
candidates.data_to_find: KBA monthly press-release schedule and definitions for 2026; exact scope of 'Neuzulassungen von Personenkraftwagen' versus 'Kraftfahrzeuge insgesamt'; historical first reported versus revised September values; inclusion of motorhomes, imports, and commercial holders. Minimum evidence: current KBA definition page and release calendar.
search_hints: KBA monthly press release schedule 2026 vehicle registrations

directions.hypothesis: The missing August 2025 monthly level blocks a direct series_auto/yoy_scaling route. Finding the full 2025 monthly KBA Pkw series would let the model use observed year-on-year growth for August 2026 instead of proxying September momentum from p239.
directions.data_to_find: KBA/VDIK monthly Pkw new registrations for August 2025 and all months of 2025; preferably first-release KBA table.

directions.hypothesis: The September annual share a1 is the largest uncertainty in the annual-forecast route. Historical September shares of annual German Pkw registrations would validate or narrow a1 and test whether September 2025 was exceptional.
directions.data_to_find: Monthly and annual German Pkw new registrations 2010-2025 to compute September share of annual totals.

directions.hypothesis: August 2026 ifo Kfz-Gewerbe or ZDK dealer order-backlog data could discriminate between the seasonal August-to-September route and the annual-share route, especially around EV subsidy effects.
directions.data_to_find: ifo Kfz-Gewerbe business climate and order backlog for August 2026; ZDK monthly dealer survey for August/early September 2026.

assessment.note: All report September 2025 German Pkw new registrations near 235,528. They mostly republish KBA or VDA/KBA-derived figures, so they are not independent; p213 rounds to 235,500 and p335 to 235,527. Kept as a strong level anchor.
September 2025 year-on-year growth is consistently about +12.8% (p214 rounds to +13%). Same underlying KBA source.
September 2025 was +13.7% vs August 2025. This is the month-on-month seasonal factor used in m1, but it is a single-year observation and may be distorted by August 2025 base effects.
Commercial share of September 2025 Pkw registrations is 65.8% across KBA-derived copies; definition and period align.
Private Pkw registrations in September 2025 grew +17.1% year on year; consistent across KBA and trade-press extracts.
BEV registrations in September 2025 are consistently 45,495; same KBA measurement, so not independent confirmation beyond the KBA source.
August 2026 Pkw new registrations are 212,563 across VDA/KBA table copies. p239 adds +2.6% year-on-year; p288's table rounds the growth to +3%. These are the latest pre-cutoff monthly anchors.
August 2026 BEV registrations are 68,930 and 32.4% share. Same KBA/VDA source; useful for powertrain mix but not for total level.
VDA's 2026 German Pkw forecast is 2.90 million, +2% vs 2025. Multiple outlets republish the same VDA forecast, so they are one source, not independent forecast evidence.

ZDK forecast is slightly higher at about 2.95 million (+3.5% to +4%). It is a different industry association and broadly supports a modest-growth 2026 market, but is not directly used because it lacks a September split.

Volkswagen Group assumes the German 2026 market at prior-year level, weaker than VDA's +2% and ZDK's +3.5-4%. It is a qualitative group planning assumption, not a KBA-compatible forecast, so it is a downside cross-check rather than a level substitute.
p176 labels September 2025 as 10.4% of January-September 2025, but p1/p4 imply about 11.2% (235,528/2,110,348). The point is mislabeled or arithmetically inconsistent, so it is discarded.

September 2023 was 224,502 and fell -17.9% vs August 2023, while September 2025 rose +13.7% vs August 2025. Different years and policy/seasonal conditions; not a contradiction, but evidence that August-September month-on-month factors are unstable.
September 2024 was 208,848, down 7% year on year; September 2025 at 235,528 then fits the reported +12.8% recovery. Levels and changes are internally consistent.

p303 is December 2025 month-on-month change, not the 2025 annual level; p305 gives full-year 2025 growth +1.4%. The 2025 annual total appears only inside p303's quoted table, so it is not used as a direct level id.
ifo automotive indicators show improving expectations but a still-negative current situation. They are qualitative demand context, not a September registration level.

German EV purchase subsidies and extended tax exemption support BEV demand in 2026. They may explain the strong August 2026 BEV share but do not provide a total-Pkw registration level or a quantified September timing shift.

extra_directions.hypothesis: The missing August 2025 monthly level blocks a direct series_auto/yoy_scaling route. Finding the full 2025 monthly KBA Pkw series would let the model use observed year-on-year growth for August 2026 instead of proxying September momentum from p239.
extra_directions.data_to_find: KBA/VDIK monthly Pkw new registrations for August 2025 and all months of 2025; preferably first-release KBA table.

extra_directions.hypothesis: The September annual share a1 is the largest uncertainty in the annual-forecast route. Historical September shares of annual German Pkw registrations would validate or narrow a1 and test whether September 2025 was exceptional.
extra_directions.data_to_find: Monthly and annual German Pkw new registrations 2010-2025 to compute September share of annual totals.

extra_directions.hypothesis: August 2026 ifo Kfz-Gewerbe or ZDK dealer order-backlog data could discriminate between the seasonal August-to-September route and the annual-share route, especially around EV subsidy effects.
extra_directions.data_to_find: ifo Kfz-Gewerbe business climate and order backlog for August 2026; ZDK monthly dealer survey for August/early September 2026.

p238.role: August 2026 new Pkw registrations in Germany, monthly level (vehicle/month)

p3.role: September 2025 vs August 2025 month-on-month growth rate, used as the August-to-September seasonal factor

methods.rationale: Applies the latest observed monthly level to the most recent pre-cutoff August-to-September seasonal move. Shared dependency: p238 and p3 are both KBA/VDA-based. Failure mode: the 2025 August-to-September factor may be distorted by the low August 2025 base or EV pull-forward; p15 shows the same month-on-month factor can be strongly negative in other years.

p1.role: September 2025 new Pkw registrations in Germany, monthly level (vehicle/month)

p239.role: August 2026 year-on-year growth rate, used as a proxy for September 2026 year-on-year growth

methods.rationale: Anchors on September 2025 and carries forward the latest observed year-on-year momentum. VDA's +2% annual forecast and August 2026 +2.6% YoY support a modest positive growth assumption. Failure mode: August and September YoY growth can diverge because of model launches, EV subsidy timing, or working-day differences, so this is a momentum proxy, not a direct September observation.

p50.role: VDA 2026 annual German Pkw new-registration forecast (vehicle/year)

a1.role: September share of annual German Pkw new registrations (fraction)

methods.rationale: Converts the independent VDA annual forecast into a September count using a seasonal share. The forecast vintage is before the cutoff, and a1 is based on the 2025 KBA September level relative to the 2025 annual total shown in kept evidence. Failure modes: VDA and KBA definitions may not be identical; the September share may shift because of subsidy-induced pull-forward or a different model-cycle pattern. The unit is the September vehicle count because a1 allocates the annual total to the target month.

assumptions.name: September share of annual German Pkw registrations, 2026
assumptions.rationale: September is typically a mid-to-strong month but not a year-end peak. The 2025 September level of 235,528 (p1) against the 2025 annual total of 2,857,591 shown in p303's KBA table implies about 8.2%. September 2026 has a similar weekday count to September 2025, so no large calendar shift is assumed. The range reflects historical variation and possible EV-subsidy timing effects.
assumptions.applies_when: The VDA 2026 annual forecast p50 is comparable to KBA Pkw Neuzulassungen and September 2026 has a normal seasonal share.

The best estimate for new passenger car (Pkw) registrations in Germany during September 2026 is [[estimate]] [[unit]] ([[interval_level]] interval [[p10]] to [[p90]] [[unit]]).

Two routes were combined with equal weight. The short-term route anchors on [[p186_value]] for September 2024, applies the September 2025 change of [[p2_value]], then carries the level forward by the average of the July 2026 change ([[p137_value]]) and August 2026 change ([[p239_value]]), giving [[m1_estimate]] [[unit]] at weight [[m1_weight]]. The top-down route multiplies the VDA 2026 forecast of [[p50_value]] by an assumed September share of [[a1_value]] (range [[a1_low]] to [[a1_high]]), giving [[m2_estimate]] [[unit]] at weight [[m2_weight]].

The observed anchors are historical; the forward momentum and the September share are transfers and assumptions, not observations. The interval is conditional on those assumptions. The main risk is that September 2026 momentum or seasonality departs from the assumed pattern. The most useful missing evidence would be early September 2026 order or registration data.

Unit of the estimate: [[unit_full]].

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a1 September share of annual German Pkw registrations, 2026: [[a1_value]], range [[a1_low]] to [[a1_high]] (range widened by code); used by m2. Overturned by: A material VDA forecast revision, a large September-specific policy pull-forward or delay, or a clearly abnormal September working-day pattern.

Method details (computed by code):
- m1 formula_mc: p186 * (1 + p2) * (1 + mean(p137, p239)); Monte Carlo P10 to P90 [[m1_mc_p10]] to [[m1_mc_p90]]; result unit (vehicle/month) * 1 month converted to vehicle; own 80% width [[m1_width]] (no error evidence, code's default width)
- m2 formula_mc: p50 * a1; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 [[m2_mc_p10]] to [[m2_mc_p90]]; result unit (vehicle/month) * 1 month converted to vehicle; own 80% width [[m2_width]] (Monte Carlo of the formula inputs)
- Combination: [[n_blocks]] block(s), equal weight per block (methods whose inputs overlap by at least half form one block; backtest errors set widths, not weights): B1 = m1: [[block1_value]] (width [[block1_width]], no error evidence, code's default width); B2 = m2: [[block2_value]] (width [[block2_width]], Monte Carlo of the formula inputs). Estimate = the geometric mean of the two blocks.
- Interval: root mean square of the block widths [[blocks_rms_width]]; Birge ratio [[birge_ratio]] (not above one, so no widening); final width [[final_width]].
final.text:
The best estimate for new passenger car (Pkw) registrations in Germany during September 2026 is 238,698 vehicle (80% model-based interval 166,918 to 341,346 vehicle).

Two routes were combined with equal weight. The short-term route anchors on 208,848 new passenger car for September 2024, applies the September 2025 change of 12.8%, then carries the level forward by the average of the July 2026 change (1.2%) and August 2026 change (2.6%), giving 240,003 vehicle at weight 50%. The top-down route multiplies the VDA 2026 forecast of 2,900,000 new passenger car (vehicle) by an assumed September share of 8.2% (range 5.787% to 11.57%), giving 237,399 vehicle at weight 50%.

The observed anchors are historical; the forward momentum and the September share are transfers and assumptions, not observations. The interval is conditional on those assumptions. The main risk is that September 2026 momentum or seasonality departs from the assumed pattern. The most useful missing evidence would be early September 2026 order or registration data.

Unit of the estimate: vehicle (new passenger car (vehicle); total for 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-30).

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a1 September share of annual German Pkw registrations, 2026: 8.2%, range 5.787% to 11.57% (range widened by code); used by m2. Overturned by: A material VDA forecast revision, a large September-specific policy pull-forward or delay, or a clearly abnormal September working-day pattern.

Method details (computed by code):
- m1 formula_mc: p186 * (1 + p2) * (1 + mean(p137, p239)); Monte Carlo P10 to P90 199,849 to 289,291; result unit (vehicle/month) * 1 month converted to vehicle; own 80% width x/÷1.38 (no error evidence, code's default width)
- m2 formula_mc: p50 * a1; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 160,757 to 351,718; result unit (vehicle/month) * 1 month converted to vehicle; own 80% width x/÷1.48 (Monte Carlo of the formula inputs)
- Combination: 2 block(s), equal weight per block (methods whose inputs overlap by at least half form one block; backtest errors set widths, not weights): B1 = m1: 240,003 (width x/÷1.38, no error evidence, code's default width); B2 = m2: 237,399 (width x/÷1.48, Monte Carlo of the formula inputs). Estimate = the geometric mean of the two blocks.
- Interval: root mean square of the block widths x/÷1.43; Birge ratio 0.03 (not above one, so no widening); final width x/÷1.43.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
